canonical_source.selection: Complete source-only release selected as one coherent edition. Project Madurai commentary releases pmuni0490_01, pmuni0523_01, pmuni0523_02, and pmuni0534 are separate editions and are not merged.

evidence_classification.canonical: printed by canonical Project Madurai source
evidence_classification.mechanical: derived only for parsing, source-order identity, hashes, or file navigation

unnumbered_literary_text.classification: unnumbered invocation preserved in full-text.md; no 000.md is created

source_grammar.normal_pattern: HTML table record; first cell is the printed record number, middle cells contain BR-delimited verse, right cells contain line-end numbers
source_grammar.number_heading_pattern: bare integer in the first table cell; no poem-level tiṇai, context, or poet appears
source_grammar.heading_punctuation_variants: spacing around the bare number varies; no semantic punctuation variant
source_grammar.numeric_line_end_markers: printed in separate layout cells and excluded from literary bodies
html_anomalies: Record 174 begins as a new table row without a new opening table tag and is parsed from the repeated number/body-cell grammar.
Records 131 and 319 carry duplicated printed number labels 130 and 318 respectively.
source_grammar.source_part_grammar_differences: none; all three divisions use the same table grammar

textual_conditions.ellipsis_policy: Preserved exactly. The source gives no explicit loss statement, so these are not automatically classified as lacunae; their typographic or textual force remains unresolved.

structural_strategy: Three section files reproduce the three source-printed macro-divisions. No mechanical fifty-poem ranges, பத்து groups, or number-derived tiṇai classification are asserted.
unresolved_ambiguities: The canonical identity of source-order records 131 and 319 is mechanically derived from continuous source order; their duplicated printed labels are preserved verbatim and reported.
The two printed ASCII ellipses are preserved but not interpreted as explicit textual loss because the source supplies no loss statement.
